dossier_meta.statement_text: There exists an absolute constant $a>0$ such that, for all $3$-graphs $G$ and $H$, $r^{p}(G,H)\geq r(G,H)^{a}$ whenever $p>r(G,H)^{o(1)}$.
dossier_meta.context_text: The authors introduce the notion of pair constructions $\chi_{f,g}$ of complexity $p$, observing that stepping-up and inducibility constructions both fit this paradigm. They conjecture that any Ramsey coloring of order $N$ yields one of order $N^{\Omega(1)}$ with much smaller complexity, which would explain the prevalence of low-complexity constructions in Ramsey theory and potentially illuminate the possible growth rates of $r(H, K_{n}^{(3)})$.
